sn35.229:1.1: “Bhikkhus, the uninstructed worldling speaks of ‘the ocean, the ocean.’
sn35.229:1.2: But that is not the ocean in the Noble One’s Discipline;
sn35.229:1.3: that is only a great mass of water, a great body of water.
sn35.229:1.4: “There are, bhikkhus, forms cognizable by the eye that are desirable, lovely, agreeable, pleasing, sensually enticing, tantalizing.
sn35.229:1.5: This is called the ocean in the Noble One’s Discipline.
sn35.229:1.6: Here this world with its devas, Mara, and Brahma, this generation with its ascetics and brahmins, its devas and humans, for the most part is submerged, become like a tangled skein, like a knotted ball of thread, like matted reeds and rushes, and cannot pass beyond the plane of misery, the bad destinations, the nether world, saṁsara.
sn35.229:2.1: “There are sounds cognizable by the ear … mental phenomena cognizable by the mind that are desirable, lovely, agreeable, pleasing, sensually enticing, tantalizing.
sn35.229:2.3: Here this world with its devas, Mara, and Brahma, this generation with its ascetics and brahmins, its devas and humans, for the most part is submerged, become like a tangled skein, like a knotted ball of thread, like matted reeds and rushes, and cannot pass beyond the plane of misery, the bad destinations, the nether world, saṁsara.
sn35.229:3.1: “One who has expunged lust and hate Along with the taint of ignorance,
sn35.229:3.2: Has crossed this ocean so hard to cross
sn35.229:3.4: With its dangers of sharks, demons, waves.
sn35.229:4.2: Has abandoned suffering for no renewed existence.
sn35.229:4.3: Passed away, he cannot be measured,
sn35.229:4.4: I say: He has bewildered the King of Death.”
